items.rationale: The theft-damaged frame is covered at its pre-loss specification under 7.1.7 and 7.1.9. The €229 gross estimate takes a rateable share of the €500 mobility limit under 4.2.2 (€500 / €1,080).
Replacing the theft-damaged brakes is covered under 7.1.7(b). The €140 gross estimate is multiplied by the rateable factor of €500 / €1,080 under 4.2.2.
Under 4.2.3, the tracker must itself be an affected item; the original worked and no damage or loss is established. If covered, €39 gross would yield about €17.43 after sharing the mobility limit.
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.5 exclude routine service on the unaffected second bike. The conditional service estimate is €120 gross.
Sections 3.1.7 and 4.2.3 exclude supplementary equipment that was not itself affected. The conditional gross estimate for the two invoiced pieces is €140.
Section 7.1.7(f) covers necessary carriage attributable to the theft repair, not shipping for the new accessories. The €26 gross estimate is multiplied by €500 / €1,080 under 4.2.2.
Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.8(f) cover the bicycle trade's attendance if required for the theft repair. The €77 gross rate is multiplied by €500 / €1,080 under 4.2.2.
Fitting the replacement assemblies is covered under 7.1.7(c), provided it is not the same work billed again as hourly labour under 7.1.8(g). The €113 gross estimate is multiplied by €500 / €1,080.

Sections 7.1.7(e) and 7.1.10 cover sundries consumed by the theft repair, but this generic line does not establish what they served. If substantiated at €15 gross, its share would be €15 × €500 / €1,095.

Section 7.1.7(d) covers the invoiced apprentice hour if attributable to the theft repair rather than the second bike's service or work already billed as assembly. The €55 gross rate is multiplied by €500 / €1,080.
Sections 7.1.7(d) and 7.1.8(g) cover one skilled hour of theft repair if not already billed as assembly. The €54 full gross rate is multiplied by €500 / €1,080.
The initial locksmith attendance was necessary and is independently covered under 5.2.2(a). The €50 gross call-out estimate is multiplied by €500 / €1,080.
Section 5.2.2(b) expressly covers cutting and removing the lock to release the bicycle. Both invoiced pieces are retained: 2 × €54 × €500 / €1,080.
Sections 5.2.2(a) and 7.1.8(f) require the second attendance to be necessary for recovery; the claim establishes no need for it. If substantiated, €50 gross would yield €50 × €500 / €1,130.
The yard made payment a condition of release, so the fee is covered under 5.2.2(c), not excluded as administration. The €100 fee plus 19% VAT is €119 gross, multiplied by €500 / €1,080 under 4.2.2.
Sections 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(d) exclude claim-processing charges; this is separate from the yard's mandatory release fee. The conditional gross estimate for the flat fee is €15.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers every labour grade used to release the bike, subject to the duplicate-charge rule in 7.1.8(g). The €55 gross rate for one hour is multiplied by €500 / €1,080.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers the skilled hour used for recovery if it was not already included in the lock-removal charge. The €54 full gross rate is multiplied by €500 / €1,080.
